config.title: Build data retention cleanup task

intro.title: Build data retention cleanup task
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a data retention cleanup task using Node.js. You will create a script that automatically deletes old data from a simulated database to comply with data retention policies. The core programming concept is using timers and scheduling with setInterval to run periodic cleanup operations. You will work with JavaScript Date objects to compare record ages and implement a simple filtering logic to remove outdated entries. This exercise introduces you to backend automation and managing data lifecycle in Node.js applications.
intro.usecase: Data retention cleanup tasks are essential in applications that handle user-generated content, logs, or temporary files to comply with privacy regulations and optimize storage. For example, social media platforms automatically delete old direct messages after a set period, while e-commerce systems purge expired shopping cart data to free up database space. In healthcare applications, patient records might be anonymized after legal retention periods expire. Developers implement these scheduled cleanup jobs using cron jobs or task schedulers to maintain system performance and ensure regulatory compliance without manual intervention.

objectives: Construct a scheduled cleanup task using Node.js cron jobs
Implement file system operations to identify and remove outdated data files
Configure retention policies based on file age and naming patterns
Initialize logging mechanisms to track cleanup task execution and errors
Integrate environment variables to customize retention periods and file paths
Manipulate directory structures to safely archive or delete expired data
Apply error handling to manage file permission issues and missing directories

steps.title: Define the calculateCutoffDate function
steps.instruction: Create a function named calculateCutoffDate that calculates the cutoff date by subtracting RETENTION_DAYS from the current date and returns that date.
steps.hint: You can create a new Date object for the current date, then use setDate() to subtract the retention days. Return the resulting Date object.
steps.expectedOutcome: The calculateCutoffDate function should be defined and return a Date object representing the cutoff date.
successCriteria: A function named calculateCutoffDate is created that uses RETENTION_DAYS and returns a Date object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function subtracts RETENTION_DAYS from the current date and returns the resulting Date object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The calculateCutoffDate function is missing or doesn't correctly calculate the cutoff date. Review how to subtract days from a Date object.

steps.title: Add file age checking logic
steps.instruction: Inside the cleanupOldFiles function, add logic to check if each file's last modified date is older than the cutoff date.
steps.hint: You'll need to compare the file's mtime (modification time) with the cutoff date. Use the Date object for comparison.
steps.expectedOutcome: The cleanupOldFiles function will have logic to compare each file's modification time with the cutoff date.
successCriteria: The function contains code that checks if a file's last modified date is older than the cutoff date.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Add file deletion logic
steps.instruction: Inside the cleanupOldFiles function, after the file age checking logic comment, add code to delete files that are older than the retention period.
steps.hint: You'll need to iterate through the files array, check each file's stats to get its modification time, compare it with the cutoffDate, and use fs.unlink to delete old files.
steps.expectedOutcome: The cleanupOldFiles function will now include logic to identify and delete files older than the retention period.

steps.title: Set up the scheduled task
steps.instruction: Use node-cron's schedule method to run the cleanupOldFiles function daily at midnight (cron pattern '0 0 * * *').
steps.hint: Call cron.schedule() with the cron pattern as the first argument and your cleanup function as the second argument.
steps.expectedOutcome: The cleanup function will be scheduled to run automatically every day at midnight.
successCriteria: cron.schedule is called with pattern '0 0 * * *' and cleanupOldFiles as the callback.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling cron.schedule with the correct cron pattern and passing cleanupOldFiles as the callback.
